memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Stay in this land for a while, and I will be with you and will bless you. For to you and your descendants I will give all these lands and will confirm the oath I swore to your father Abraham. I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and will give them all these lands, and through your offspring all nations on earth will be blessed, because Abraham obeyed me and did everything I required of him, keeping my commands, my decrees and my instructions.'" - Gen 26:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God renews to Isaac the great promises He had made to Abraham — descendants like the stars, a land, and a blessing that would reach every nation on earth. These were covenant promises tied to Abraham's family and to the land God had chosen, and God was faithfully carrying them forward to the next generation.

At the heart of it all shines one line: "I will be with you." That is the promise that never changes. Whatever specific covenant God made with Abraham's family, His unchanging character is to be present with His people who trust Him.

Notice too the phrase, "through your offspring all nations on earth will be blessed." This was pointing beyond Isaac to one particular descendant — Jesus Christ. Through Him, the blessing has now reached the whole world, and all who belong to Christ share in Abraham's blessing (Gal 3:8, 16, 29). What was promised long ago has come true in the gospel.

God mentions Abraham's obedience, but remember: Abraham's obedience grew out of his faith in a God who had first made him promises by grace (Gen 15:6). We do not earn God's presence; we receive it by trusting Him. The same faithful God who was with Abraham and Isaac is with His people still.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I rest in the promise that God is "with me"?
2. Am I trusting God's grace, or trying to earn His favour?
3. How does it move me that the blessing reached all nations through Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that in Christ the promise to bless all nations has come true. Thank You that You are with me. Help me to trust You as Abraham did. Amen.
